naturalness: Wording frequently obscures the intended meaning.
The message is recoverable, but recurring awkward constructions impede it.
Most wording is usable; several expressions could be more idiomatic.
Wording is consistently natural, with only minor awkwardness.
Expressions are idiomatic and flexibly adapted to the learner's meaning.
workplace_tone: Wording repeatedly works against the communication purpose or relationship.
Several wording choices are too abrupt, vague, or mismatched in formality.
Wording is broadly appropriate, with a clear opportunity to adjust warmth or directness.
Word choice, directness, and formality consistently suit the situation.
Wording is well judged and adapts to the other participant's responses.

purposes.title: Welcome everyone
purposes.expression: Good to see everyone. Thanks for making the time today.
purposes.alternative: Hi everyone, glad you could make it.
purposes.explanation: Acknowledge the people and appreciate their time before getting down to work.
purposes.example: Good to see everyone. Thanks for making the time today. Let's look at the project timeline.
purposes.hint_starter: Good to see everyone. Thanks for…
purposes.preset_situation: You are opening a weekly team meeting with colleagues about a shared project.
purposes.tutor_role: Alex, a teammate attending the meeting
purposes.communication_goal: Welcome the group appropriately, acknowledge their time, and introduce a clear purpose; adapt naturally to a colleague's response.
purposes.opening_direction: Alex is an attendee. Say the group is ready, then ask the learner, the host, a direct question inviting them to open the meeting, such as 'Could you get us started?' Alex must not welcome the group himself.

purposes.title: Set the agenda
purposes.expression: The goal today is to agree on our next steps.
purposes.alternative: Let's work out what happens next.
purposes.explanation: Name the intended outcome so colleagues know what the discussion needs to achieve.
purposes.example: The goal today is to agree on our next steps for the launch.
purposes.preset_situation: Explain the goal and intended outcome of a project discussion.
purposes.communication_goal: Introduce the topic and a specific outcome, then invite a contribution.
purposes.opening_direction: Alex is an attendee. Ask the learner, the host, what the meeting should achieve today. The learner answers by setting the agenda and intended outcome; Alex must not set it himself.

purposes.title: Wrap up
purposes.expression: Before we wrap up, let's confirm who's doing what.
purposes.alternative: Let's quickly check our next steps.
purposes.explanation: Signal the end of the discussion and make responsibilities clear.
purposes.example: Before we wrap up, let's confirm who's doing what. I'll send the notes today.
purposes.preset_situation: Close a team discussion and confirm next steps.
purposes.communication_goal: Confirm decisions, owners, and next steps before thanking the group.
purposes.opening_direction: The discussion is ending. Alex asks the learner, the host, a direct question about the agreed next steps. The learner answers by summarizing decisions and assigning responsibilities. Do not summarize or close on behalf of the learner.

purposes.title: Share progress
purposes.expression: I've made some progress on the project timeline.
purposes.explanation: Name the work and a concrete change to make your update easy to follow.
purposes.example: I've made some progress on the project timeline. The first draft is ready to review.
purposes.preset_situation: Give a concise project update in a weekly check-in.
purposes.communication_goal: Explain what changed, what remains, and the next step.
purposes.opening_direction: Alex is the manager. Ask a direct question about progress on the learner's work within an allowed variation, then let the learner answer.

purposes.title: Ask for support
purposes.expression: I could use your help with prioritizing the next steps.
purposes.alternative: Could we work out the priorities together?
purposes.explanation: A specific request helps your colleague understand what support would be useful.
purposes.example: I could use your help with prioritizing the next steps. Two deadlines overlap.
purposes.hint_starter: I could use your help with…
purposes.preset_situation: Explain a blocker and make a specific request for help.
purposes.communication_goal: Explain a blocker, request specific help, and agree on a next step.
purposes.opening_direction: The learner needs support on the learner's work. Alex asks a direct question about what help they need, then waits for their answer. Alex must not request help from the learner.

purposes.title: Ask for feedback
purposes.expression: I'd appreciate your feedback on how I structured the update.
purposes.alternative: What could I make clearer next time?
purposes.explanation: Identify a specific part of your work so the other person can give useful feedback.
purposes.example: I'd appreciate your feedback on how I structured the update. Was the next step clear?
purposes.preset_situation: Ask for specific feedback on a recent piece of work.
purposes.tutor_role: Alex, a colleague who reviewed your work
purposes.communication_goal: Invite specific feedback and clarify how to act on it.
purposes.opening_direction: Alex has reviewed the learner's work. Ask a direct question about which part they would like feedback on. The learner answers by requesting specific feedback. Do not ask them to evaluate Alex's work.

purposes.title: Start a conversation
purposes.alternative: How has your week been so far?
purposes.explanation: An open, everyday question gives a colleague room to choose what to share.
purposes.example: Hi Alex, good to see you. How's your morning going?
purposes.preset_situation: Begin a friendly conversation before work starts.
purposes.communication_goal: Begin a friendly exchange by responding to the colleague and asking a question back.
purposes.opening_direction: Alex meets the learner at the coffee area or before a meeting. Alex asks first with a simple everyday question, such as how their morning is going. The learner answers and can ask a friendly question back. Do not wait for the learner to speak first.

purposes.title: Follow up
purposes.expression: What was the most interesting part?
purposes.explanation: Follow something your colleague said and invite a little more detail.
purposes.example: I'm glad the presentation went well. What was the most interesting part?
purposes.preset_situation: Ask about a presentation your colleague mentioned earlier.
purposes.tutor_role: Alex, who just gave a presentation
purposes.communication_goal: Recall the earlier event and ask a relevant follow-up.
purposes.opening_direction: Alex briefly mentions the presentation or demonstration he just gave, then asks what the learner would like to know about it. The learner answers by asking a relevant follow-up. Do not ask that follow-up on their behalf.

purposes.title: Close a conversation
purposes.expression: It was good catching up. I'd better get back to work.
purposes.alternative: I'll let you get on. Let's catch up again soon.
purposes.explanation: Acknowledge the chat and give a simple reason to leave without sounding abrupt.
purposes.example: It was good catching up. I'd better get back to work. See you at lunch.
purposes.preset_situation: End a friendly chat when it is time to return to work.
purposes.communication_goal: Bring the chat to a friendly close and respond appropriately to the farewell.
purposes.opening_direction: After a pleasant chat, Alex asks a direct question about whether the learner needs to get back to work or their next meeting. The learner answers by closing politely. Do not say the learner's farewell for them.
